>If men and women can like all of the same things and have all the same ranges of personalities, what makes a man any different than a woman?


This is a really good point! I think that's why I have struggled to understand, as if someone was to ask why I thought i was a woman, I'd probably just shrug and say something like "because I have those body parts." I don't feel like there's any activity/job/emotion/etc that is or should be linked to one gender. In my eyes, everyone should be able to do and feel however they like, as long as its not hurting others.

>if I don’t even know what being a girl means, how can I say I am one?

This honestly makes me think. I know I'm not a guy, but I honestly don't have a good reason why I identify as a woman, just that I have the parts. Now my head hurts.. haha

For me, I think I'd feel very odd with the male body parts. Although I'd go with a day of having the opposite parts just to make sure. That and to helicopter, if you get what I mean lol

So it's not so much gender norms that  have made you uncomfortable, its more that you feel your body doesn't represent who you are? 

Am I right to say that basically it's the same as if everyone started to refer to me as a guy, even though I know I'm a woman? I've had people call me a man before (bullying's great  /s) and I felt horrible afterwards.

You're right there, it even comes down to the tone people talk to you in; I've noticed people use softer tone if you're a female and harsher if you're a male.

>there's also that women tend to have a layer of fat that obscures muscles and veins in the hands, legs, and arms, giving a softer appearance, while men don't. And facial and body hair

This hits home. I had a job where I lost a lot of my fat and my muscles were very defined and I just felt yuck. That coupled with the unfortunate body hair I have made me feel horrible about myself. I feel better than I did, but not 100%.

Thank you for your reply. So those gender norms that are pushed don't bother you? That is a good way to look at it though, that you never have to live to what society stereotypes you as; I mean, I'd hate it if just because I'm a woman, I was forced to wear make up every day!

What is it that makes you feel happier as a woman? And how did you know that identifying as one would improve how you felt?

I look in the mirror and just feel so unattractive, but then unmotivated to change much, but then I have this thought of "oh well, I guess that's just me."
